steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 protect individuals' personal data. Organisations must have a lawful basis to process data and must obtain consent in most cases.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Individual rights under UK GDPR: right of access, right to rectification, right to erasure (right to be forgotten), right to restrict processing, right to data portability, and right to object.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Online Safety Act 2023 requires platforms to protect users from harmful content, especially children. Ofcom has enforcement powers including fines of up to 10% of global revenue.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Freedom of expression online is protected by Article 10 ECHR but has limits: hate speech, harassment, defamation, incitement to violence, and terrorism promotion are illegal.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always link digital rights to traditional rights — privacy, free expression, protection from harm Use specific legislation names: UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, Online Safety Act 2023 The freedom vs safety debate is a key AO2 topic — always present both sides and reach a conclusion
